newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Hurd says EU must do more on eastward expansion.
newsitem.headline: Hurd says EU must do more on eastward expansion.

text.p: Former British Foreign Secretary Douglas Hurd criticised the European Union on Wednesday for not doing enough to prepare for the eventual expansion of the union to central and eastern Europe.
Speaking at a banking conference in Prague, Hurd, who is now deputy chairman of London-based NatWest Markets, said existing members had not yet tackled the major issues facing expansion.
"We have not done enough to prepare for the enlargement that must come," Hurd told the conference. "The burden of work for enlargement should now fall on existing (EU) members."
Hurd said four countries of the former Communist bloc -- the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland and Slovenia -- have made great strides in democratic reforms to prepare for eventual EU entry.
But he said the union itself had not begun to deal with the sensitive issues of reforming the common agriculture policy (CAP), and other Brussels-based subsidy programmes.
He added that Brussels was good at giving advice, but was not as good at getting its own house in order.
